title: Technology
description: Words for essays and discussions about the internet, artificial intelligence, social media and digital life.

words.definition: the use of machines and computers to do work previously done by people
words.example: Automation has replaced many routine jobs in factories and warehouses.

words.definition: the ability of computers to perform tasks that normally need human intelligence
words.example: Artificial intelligence is already used to detect diseases in medical scans.

words.definition: the most modern and advanced
words.example: The new hospital is equipped with cutting-edge diagnostic technology.

words.definition: no longer used because something newer exists
words.example: Smartphones have made many devices, such as alarm clocks and maps, almost obsolete.

words.definition: a new idea, method or product, or the process of creating it
words.example: Government funding can encourage innovation in small technology firms.

words.definition: the right to keep your personal life and information to yourself
words.example: Many users are unaware of how much their privacy is compromised by free apps.

words.definition: criminal activity carried out using computers or the internet
words.example: Online banking has brought convenience but also a rise in cybercrime.

words.definition: the gap between people who have access to modern technology and those who do not
words.example: Providing cheap internet in rural areas would help to close the digital divide.

words.definition: making people want to do or use something repeatedly
words.example: Social media apps are deliberately designed to be addictive.

words.definition: easy to use or understand
words.example: Older people are more likely to adopt technology that is genuinely user-friendly.

words.definition: an important discovery or development
words.example: Battery technology is waiting for a breakthrough that would make electric cars cheaper.

words.definition: careful watching of people, often by the police or government
words.example: The growth of camera surveillance in public places raises questions about civil liberties.

words.definition: false or misleading information
words.example: Misinformation spreads much faster on social media than corrections do.

words.definition: a small, clever device or tool
words.example: Children today grow up surrounded by electronic gadgets.

words.definition: the ability to connect to the internet or other devices
words.example: Poor connectivity in remote islands makes online learning difficult.

words.definition: time spent looking at a phone, computer or television screen
words.example: Paediatricians recommend limiting screen time for children under five.

words.definition: a set of rules a computer follows to solve a problem or make a decision
words.example: Streaming platforms use algorithms to recommend films based on viewing history.

words.definition: buying and selling goods and services online
words.example: The rapid growth of e-commerce has forced many small shops to close.

words.definition: the state of needing something in order to function
words.example: Our growing dependence on smartphones may be weakening our memory.

words.definition: to change something completely and fundamentally
words.example: Mobile payments have revolutionised the way people shop in Southeast Asia.

words.definition: the process of changing information into a code to keep it secure
words.example: Strong encryption protects messages from being read by hackers.

words.definition: created by computers or existing online rather than physically
words.example: Virtual meetings have reduced the need for business travel.

words.definition: knowing a lot about modern technology and how to use it
words.example: Younger employees are often more tech-savvy than their managers.

words.definition: to fail to work correctly
words.example: A software error caused the traffic lights to malfunction across the city.

words.definition: affecting someone's private life in an unwelcome way
words.example: Many people find targeted online advertising intrusive.

words.definition: to make a process simpler and more efficient
words.example: Online forms have streamlined the process of applying for a passport.

words.definition: designed to be worn on the body, such as a smartwatch
words.example: Wearable devices allow users to monitor their heart rate and sleep.

words.definition: a person who gains access to computer systems without permission
words.example: Hackers stole the personal details of millions of customers.

words.definition: storing and processing data on remote servers accessed through the internet
words.example: Cloud computing allows small companies to use powerful software without buying servers.

words.definition: never having happened or existed before
words.example: The internet gives ordinary people unprecedented access to information.
